title: Notosan — scroll-driven nature parallax hero
notes: Travel site hero for a fictional Japanese nature park brand, "Notosan." Originally analyzed as a 10s auto-advancing carousel, but that recreation felt static/choppy in practice. This prompt is the corrected version: a real scroll-driven parallax build (three normal-flow 100vh sections + fixed crossfaded background layers + IntersectionObserver reveals), validated end-to-end and confirmed fluid.
recreation_prompt:
Build a scroll-driven, multi-section hero for a fictional Japanese nature-park travel brand called "Notosan." The page has THREE full-height sections the user scrolls through normally (this is not a fixed/absolute-stacked single-screen carousel) — each section swaps in its own full-viewport background photo and reveals its own heading/copy as it scrolls into view.

GLOBAL LAYOUT:
- `html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }`. Body is black, white text, `overflow-x: hidden`.
- Fixed navbar pinned to the top of the whole page (not per-section): wordmark "Notosan" on the left; nav links "Community / About / Support / Contact" plus a pill-shaped "Register" button (1px white border, fills white with black text on hover) on the right. Background is a gradient from `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` at the top fading to transparent, so it reads over any photo beneath it. `padding: 2rem 4rem`, `z-index: 100`.
- Typography: pair a serif display face (e.g. Playfair Display) for headings with a geometric sans (e.g. Inter) for everything else — this contrast is part of the look, don't use one font for both.

BACKGROUND LAYERS (the parallax mechanism):
- Three `position: fixed; top:0; left:0; width:100%; height:120vh; z-index:-1;` divs, one per section, each with its own `background-image` (real photography — a vibrant mountain at sunrise/dusk for section 1, a mystical blue waterfall for section 2, a glowing lush forest for section 3), `background-size: cover`, plus a `::after` dark overlay (`rgba(0,0,0,0.4)`) so white text stays legible over any photo.
- All three start at `opacity: 0` with `transition: opacity 1s ease-in-out`; only the currently-relevant one carries `.active` (`opacity: 1`) at a time — crossfade, never a hard cut or a slide.
- On scroll, apply a continuous subtle parallax drift to every background layer (not just the active one, so whichever fades in next is already correctly positioned): `scrollFraction = scrollY / (document.body.scrollHeight - windowHeight)`, `translateY = -(scrollFraction * windowHeight * 0.2)`, applied as `transform: translateY(...)`. The 120vh height (20vh taller than the viewport) is exactly what gives this drift room to move without exposing an edge.
- Track which section currently owns the background by comparing `scrollY` against each section's `offsetTop - windowHeight/2`, checked from the last section backward (so the furthest-down threshold crossed wins); only touch the DOM (`classList.add/remove('active')`) when the winning section actually changes, not on every scroll tick.

FOREGROUND SECTIONS:
- Each `<section>` is a normal, real 100vh block (`display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:center; padding: 0 10%;`) — three of them stacked in normal document flow, so the page is genuinely 300vh tall and scrolls like a regular page, not a pinned/absolute single screen.
- Section 1 (hero): no alignment override, so content sits left via the default flex stretch inside its `max-width: 600px` wrapper. Kicker-style subtitle ("Journey to new frontiers, Journey to Noto Nature Park", small, letter-spaced 3px, muted white), a massive serif headline ("VISITE", ~7rem, letter-spacing 5px, line-height 1), 2-3 lines of body copy, and a primary CTA: a transparent button with uppercase tracked text plus a circular outlined play-icon badge (50x50px) that fills white with a black icon on hover, and the whole button shifts `translateX(10px)` on hover.
- Section 2: same structure but `align-items: flex-end; text-align: right;` (content sits on the right). Small numbered tag ("02 / Experience"), serif section title ("Tranquility", ~5rem), body copy, and a secondary CTA: a plain text link ("Learn more →") whose gap between text and arrow grows from 0.8rem to 1.2rem on hover (the arrow visibly slides away, not translateX).
- Section 3: mirrors section 2 but `align-items: flex-start; text-align: left;` (back on the left). Tag ("03 / Habitat"), title ("Biodiversity"), copy, same secondary-link CTA style.

SCROLL REVEALS (IntersectionObserver, not scroll-position math):
- Each section's content wrapper starts as `opacity:0; transform: translateY(50px);` with `transition: all 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94);`.
- An `IntersectionObserver` with `{ threshold: 0.3 }` toggles a `.active` class on whichever wrapper is intersecting — add it back off every time the element leaves the viewport too, so the reveal replays if the user scrolls back up and down again, rather than firing once and staying done.
- Once `.active`, the wrapper's direct children (kicker/heading/copy/CTA) each independently run a `fadeInUp` keyframe (`opacity 0→1`, `translateY(30px)→0`, 0.8s) with staggered `animation-delay` of 0.1s/0.3s/0.5s/0.7s in DOM order, so the text cascades in piece by piece instead of arriving as one block.

RESPONSIVE: below ~768px, hide the nav links (keep logo + Register), and drop the hero title/section titles to roughly 4rem/3rem with reduced section padding.

Animate `initial={{y:-50, x:startX, opacity:0, rotate:0}}` → `animate={{y:'110vh', x:startX-100, opacity:[0,1,1,0], rotate:360}}`, linear ease, `repeat:Infinity` — falling, drifting left, fading in then out, spinning once, forever.

SECTION 2 — GAME INTRO (`min-h-screen`, `bg-[#060314]`, a soft gold radial glow at 70%/50%): two-column grid, both columns doing `whileInView` fade+slide reveals (`viewport:{once:true, margin:'-100px'}`, 0.8s). Right: a tall (600px) rounded image panel with a gold glow border showing a moody in-game/interior illustration, gradient candlelight overlay, slides in from the right 0.2s after the left column.

Cards are positioned by their index offset from the current one: `x = relativeIndex * 250px`, `z = 50 if center else -100`, `scale = 1 if center else 0.8`, `opacity = 1 center / 0.5 adjacent / 0 further`, animated with Framer Motion (`duration:0.6, ease:[0.23,1,0.32,1]`). title: Wander — travel discovery app (hero → carousel → detail)
notes: Real coded Next.js project ("WANDER" — Discover the Planet) at C:\Documents\Self Projects\website_sample_2, read component-by-component. Single-page app driven by React state (hero/carousel/detail), not routing. One gap between code and the supplied video: the checked-in DESTINATIONS array is [Grønland, Alaska, Japan, Canada, Australia], but the video's carousel frame shows Grønland/Japan/Sri Lanka/Thailand — the destination roster has evidently moved on since this was captured, so treat the list below as illustrative, not authoritative.
recreation_prompt:
Build a 3-view single-page travel app called "WANDER" (tagline "Discover the Planet"), switching between HERO → ROUTES CAROUSEL → DETAIL views via React state (not routing), animated with Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence`.

PALETTE: background #040b16 (deep navy), panel #0f172a (dark slate), accent red #dc2626, white foreground. Fonts: Inter for body text, Montserrat for display headings, and a cursive script face (e.g. Great Vibes) for one specific accent word in the hero.

NAVBAR (fixed, shared across all views): slides down on load (`y:-100→0`, 0.5s easeOut). Transparent at the top; past `scrollY>50` switches to a blurred dark bar with a bottom border and shadow. Left: a small square dark "W" mark plus "WANDER" wordmark that turns into outlined/hollow text on hover (`-webkit-text-stroke` trick, see below) with a white drop-shadow glow. Right: "About us / Search / Routes" links (each with a hover underline that grows from 0 to full width, glowing in the link's color — "Search" is styled permanently red/active, the others white) plus a circular user-avatar icon button.

VIEW 1 — HERO (`h-screen`, exclusive with the carousel view under one `AnimatePresence mode="wait"`):
- Full-bleed background photo (moody snow-capped mountains / fjord) under a flat `bg-black/30` scrim.
- "Vertical blinds" reveal on mount: 5 equal-width full-height strips in the page's background color, each `scaleY:1→0` with `transform-origin:top`, staggered 0.1s apart starting at 0.2s, 1.5s duration, easing `[0.22,1,0.36,1]` — the background photo appears to be uncovered by retracting vertical blinds rather than a simple fade.
- Stacked, overlapping display typography, centered: "DISCOVER" (black-weight, huge, fades/slides up in at delay 1s) sits behind a large rotated (-6deg) script-font "the" in accent red positioned overlapping its top-right (delay 1.4s, scale-in), which sits above "PLANET" rendered even larger directly below in hollow/outlined text (`-webkit-text-stroke:1px white; color:transparent`, delay 1.2s) — three layers of text overlapping into one lockup, each arriving on its own stagger.
- "TO BEGIN" CTA (solid red, small play-triangle icon, uppercase tracked) fades up at delay 2s; clicking it slides up a filter bar from the bottom (`y:100→0` + fade, `AnimatePresence`/exit reverses it) containing a Location dropdown, a Route-Level dropdown, two radio options ("With guide" / "Savage"), and a red "SEARCH" button that advances to the carousel view.
- Bottom overlay bar (fades in last, delay 2.5s): social links (Instagram/Facebook/Twitter as plain tracked-uppercase text) on the left, and a small decorative "audio waveform" of 5 vertical bars of varying height/opacity on the right — pure visual flourish, not a real player.

VIEW 2 — ROUTES CAROUSEL (`h-screen`, fades in/out as a whole section, `AnimatePresence` opacity 0→1→0, 0.8s):
- Faint (5% opacity) world-map image tiled behind everything.
- "ROUTES" title, small, wide-tracked, dim, at the top.
- A horizontally scrollable, scroll-snapped row of destination cards (scrollbar hidden), each a tall rounded-2xl image card that fades/slides in staggered by index. On hover: background image scales up (110%) and a bottom gradient scrim strengthens; a location-pin badge sits top-right; the destination name is always visible bottom-left, but a route-description subtitle beneath it is hidden (`translate-y-4 opacity-0`) until hover reveals it. Clicking a card advances to the detail view for that destination.
- Give each card's image and its bottom text block a shared Framer Motion `layoutId` (e.g. `image-{id}` / `content-{id}`) matching the same-keyed elements in the detail view — this is what makes the transition into the detail view feel like the card itself smoothly grows into the new layout, instead of a hard cut.
- A thin custom progress bar below the carousel fills in red proportional to horizontal scroll position (tracked via a scroll listener computing `scrollLeft/(scrollWidth-clientWidth)`).

VIEW 3 — DETAIL SPLIT-SCREEN (`fixed inset-0`, its own separate `AnimatePresence`, layered above the other two views): a left/right (stacked on mobile) 50/50 split.
- Left half: the SAME image and content block from the clicked card, via the matching shared `layoutId`s, so it visually morphs from card to full-height panel. Over it: a back-arrow button (top-left, blurred glass pill, arrow nudges left on hover) and a row of tag pills ("Extreme", "With guide", "With transport"); bottom-left shows view/like stats with icons, then a Distance/Elevation stat pair, then the destination name (huge, with a pin icon) and its route description, fading/sliding in staggered after the panel settles. A red circular floating "+" button bottom-right springs in (delay 0.5s, `type:spring, stiffness:200, damping:20`).
- Right half: a dark slate panel containing a square map area with (a) 3 faint (10% opacity) topographic squiggle-line paths as ambient background texture, (b) the real route as an SVG path: a static 10%-opacity track underneath, and an animated white dashed line drawn on top via `pathLength: 0→1` over 2s easeInOut (delay 0.8s) — the route visibly draws itself in; (c) a glowing red dot marking the start point that pops in (scale 0→1) as the line begins drawing, and (d) a pin+label marking the end point that springs in only once the line finishes (delay ~2.8s), so the sequence reads as: line draws from start to end, then the destination label arrives at the tip.

title: Jp.Travel — Japan city showcase (hover-linked backgrounds)
notes: Real coded Next.js project ("Jp.Travel") at C:\Documents\Self Projects\website_sample_3, read component-by-component (cities.ts, BackgroundTransition, HeroText, Navbar, BottomNav). One screen total, no scrolling — switching cities just swaps background/text/thumbnail state. One addition from the video not present in the raw code: every screen has a soft red circular glow (rising-sun motif) centered behind the hero text stack — HeroText.tsx as written has no such element, so it's included below as a supplement, not a literal code quote.
recreation_prompt:
Build a single fixed-viewport (`h-screen w-screen overflow-hidden`, no page scroll at all) city-showcase app called "Jp.Travel", cycling its entire background/hero through 4 Japanese cities (Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka, Nara) driven by one piece of state (`activeCityId`) — no routing, no separate pages.

PALETTE: pure black background, white foreground, one accent red #dc2626. Fonts: Inter for body/UI text, a distinctive geometric display face (e.g. Syne) for the big city names and kanji.

DECORATIVE WAVE PATTERN (exact CSS recipe, used as a 15%-opacity overlay above the background photo but below all text): three `radial-gradient`s in one `background-image`, centered at `100% 150%`, `0% 150%`, and `50% 100%` respectively, each going `transparent 20%, #fff 21%, #fff 34%, transparent 35%`, with `background-size: 60px 30px` and the third gradient offset `30px 15px` from the other two — this tiles into a traditional seigaiha (overlapping wave-scale) motif using pure CSS, no image asset.

NAVBAR (fixed top): small red circle badge with a single white letter mark, plus the "Jp.Travel" wordmark, on the left. Center: "Destinations" / "Experiences" links plus a search input that expands (`w-32→w-48`, border brightens) on focus, with a search icon anchored to its right edge. Right: plain-text social links (X / YT / IG) and a red pill "Explore" button with a soft red glow shadow.

BACKGROUND TRANSITION (the centerpiece mechanic): each city has a full-bleed photo. Only the currently-active city's image is mounted; it's revealed via a `clip-path: circle()` wipe growing from `circle(0% at 50% 100%)` to `circle(150% at 50% 100%)` — anchored at the bottom-center of the screen, so the new photo appears to bloom upward and outward from the bottom edge — over 1.2s with a custom cubic-bezier `(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1)`. The outgoing image needs no exit animation of its own; just drop it behind the incoming one in z-index the moment the new one starts. Preload every city's photo up front (on mount) so switching never shows a loading flash. A flat 40%-black scrim sits permanently over every photo for text legibility.

HERO TEXT (dead center, non-interactive except its button): a soft red circular glow (a rising-sun-style disc) sits centered directly behind the whole text stack on every city, tying the look back to the flag motif. Above it, small red-colored kanji for the active city, wide letter-spacing. Below that, the city's English name in an enormous (up to ~12rem) black-weight display font, tight tracking, heavy drop-shadow for legibility over the photo. Below that, a red "Explore {City}" button with a right-arrow icon that nudges further right on hover and whose glow intensifies on hover. On every city change, the entire text block cross-fades with a vertical slide — incoming slides up from `y:40→0`, outgoing exits sliding to `y:-40`, opacity fading both ways, ~0.6s easeOut, keyed by city id so only one is ever mounted at a time.

BOTTOM CITY SELECTOR (fixed bottom bar, black-to-transparent gradient backing): a horizontal row of circular thumbnail avatars, one per city, each with a left accent border — solid red and full opacity when that city is active, faint white at 50% opacity otherwise (brightening on hover), plus a tagline above the city name and the thumbnail image zooming in slightly on hover. Critically, switching the active city fires on `mouseenter` (hover), not just click — sweeping your cursor across the row live-previews every city's background/hero in sequence. The active city's red tint overlay on its own thumbnail should be one single shared-layout element that smoothly slides from whichever thumbnail was previously active to the new one, rather than each thumbnail independently fading its own overlay in and out.

title: Lourve — scroll-driven 3D statue museum showcase
notes: Real coded Next.js + react-three-fiber project at C:\Documents\Self Projects\website_sample_4, read component-by-component (StatueCanvas, BustModel, ContentSections, Navbar, ScrollProgress). Genuine three-way inconsistency worth flagging rather than silently resolving: the loaded 3D asset is a Nefertiti bust (/nefertiti.glb), the museum copy in ContentSections.tsx is entirely Venus de Milo facts (missing arms, Island of Melos, 1820 discovery, Louvre 1821), and the supplied video shows neither — a male Greco-Roman head/bust with a large glowing ring behind it that the code's own comment says was deliberately removed ("Removed the visible Torus geometry... but we keep the PointLights"). The mechanics below are solid and consistent across all three; pick one statue and matching facts when actually building this rather than mixing them like the source does.
recreation_prompt:
Build a scroll-driven single-page museum showcase (brand: "LOURVE") with a fixed WebGL 3D canvas (react-three-fiber / three.js) sitting behind normally-scrolling page content — the statue itself never scrolls with the page, it's animated purely by reading scroll progress each frame.

PALETTE: near-black background #050505, white foreground, one cyan accent #00f0ff, statue material near-black #0a0a0a. Fonts: Inter sans for UI/body, Playfair Display serif for headings. Background: a subtle 4-column vertical grid — one `linear-gradient` hairline (8% white opacity) repeating every 25vw across the full page.

NAVBAR (fixed top, `mix-blend-mode: difference` so it auto-inverts against whatever's behind it — statue or background): serif wordmark left; center nav links (Home/Collection/Artists/Events/Visit), with a small cyan dot indicator under whichever is active; a grip/menu icon on the right that highlights cyan on hover.

SCROLL PROGRESS RAIL (fixed to the left edge, vertically centered, also `mix-blend-difference`): one small dot per content section, dim by default and brightening to solid white when its section is active; next to the active dot, a short cyan tick mark animates into position via a spring-animated shared layout transition (jumps smoothly between dots rather than fading independently).

THE 3D CANVAS (fixed full-screen, `pointer-events:none` so scroll/clicks pass through to the real page underneath; camera at roughly z=15, fov 45; ambient + directional lighting plus a city-preset HDRI environment for reflections):
- The statue: a bust/figure rendered in a dark, glossy near-black material (low roughness ~0.3, high metalness ~0.8) so it reads as polished obsidian or dark bronze rather than plain gray plastic.
- A large glowing white ring positioned behind/around the statue at certain scroll points, acting as a dramatic halo light source (paired with a bright white point light roughly where the ring sits, plus a second cyan-tinted point light off to one side for rim lighting) — more a lit gallery spotlight ring than a solid visible object.
- BOTH the statue and the light/ring group are driven by the identical 3-phase scroll transform, read from overall page scroll progress (0→1) every animation frame:
  - Phase A (progress 0→0.4): animates from a small, centered, more face-on starting pose out to an offset "showcase" pose — moves sideways, scales up, rotates open.
  - Phase B (0.4→0.6): holds that showcase pose exactly still — a deliberate pause for the viewer to look at it.
  - Phase C (0.6→1): sweeps across to the opposite side of the screen while scaling back down slightly and rotating back toward center.
  - Never set scale/position/rotation directly from the computed target — always blend the current value toward the target with a small easing factor (~10% per frame, i.e. `current += (target - current) * 0.1`) for position, scale, AND rotation, so the statue trails smoothly behind scroll input instead of snapping to it.

CONTENT SECTIONS (normal document flow, scrolling past the fixed canvas, each revealing via `whileInView` fade/slide — use real, single-source museum-placard copy for whichever one statue you pick, not a mix):
1. Hero (100vh): centered large serif title (e.g. "Museum of Ancient Art") using mix-blend-difference for guaranteed legibility over the statue's material regardless of its tone, plus a short italic descriptive line pinned to the bottom-right corner.
2. Details (100vh): three stacked fact blocks confined to the left third of the screen (attribution/sculptor, physical dimensions, provenance/discovery), each a small serif heading over a muted uppercase caption, sliding in from the left as the section scrolls into view.
3. Story (150vh — intentionally taller than the viewport so it lingers longer): a large serif headline with one italicized emphasized word or phrase, followed by two side-by-side justified paragraphs of narrative history lower in the section, revealed with a slight delay after the headline.
